title: JACKING - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What is the proper method for raising an aircraft off the ground at multiple points during maintenance?
answer: Normal jacking procedures involve lifting one main wheel at a time.  This procedure is best accomplished using a floor jack in conjunction with the built-in jack pad . CAUTION: Jacking both wheels simultaneously at built-in jack pads is not recommended. When using built-in jack pad, flexibility of the main gear strut will cause the main wheel to slide inboard as the wheel is raised, tilting the jack. If this occurs, the jack must be lowered for a second operation.When the airplane needs to be raised off the ground at all points, the following procedure should be used.

title: JACKING - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What considerations must be made to ensure the airplane remains stable and balanced when raising it on wing jacks?
answer: Raise Airplane . (1) Place wing jacks and padded blocks under front spar, just outboard of wing strut. Ensure that padded block  is resting securely between spar and jack. (2) Raise wing jacks evenly until desired height is reached. CAUTION: When placed on jacks centered under the wing front spar, the airplane is slightly tail heavy. Tail stands must be used and weigh enough to keep the tail down under all conditions. Additionally, the tail stand must be strong enough to support any weight which might be transferred to the tailcone area during maintenance, creating a greater tail heavy condition. (3) Carefully attach tail stand to tail tiedown ring.Lower Airplane . (1) Detach tail stand from tail tiedown ring. (2) Slowly lower wing jacks simultaneously until main tires are resting on ground. (3) Remove wing jacks and pads from wing area.

question: How should the front and aft slings be positioned when lifting the airplane?
answer: The airplane may be lifted by means of suitable slings. The front sling should be hooked to each upper engine mount at the firewall, and the aft sling should be positioned around the fuselage at the first bulkhead forward of the leading edge of the stabilizer.

answer: Raise Airplane . (1) Place wing jacks and padded blocks under front spar, just outboard of wing strut. Ensure that padded block  is resting securely between spar and jack. (2) Raise wing jacks evenly until desired height is reached. CAUTION: When placed on jacks centered under the wing front spar, the airplane is slightly tail heavy. Tail stands must be used and weigh enough to keep the tail down under all conditions. Additionally, the tail stand must be strong enough to support any weight which might be transferred to the tailcone area during maintenance, creating a greater tail heavy condition. (3) Carefully attach tail stand to tail tiedown ring.Lower Airplane . (1) Detach tail stand from tail tiedown ring. (2) Slowly lower wing jacks simultaneously until main tires are resting on ground. (3) Remove wing jacks and pads from wing area.

title: JACKING - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What are the correct attachment points for the front and aft slings when lifting the airplane according to the instructions?
answer: The airplane may be lifted by means of suitable slings. The front sling should be hooked to each upper engine mount at the firewall, and the aft sling should be positioned around the fuselage at the first bulkhead forward of the leading edge of the stabilizer.

title: JACKING - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What is the proper procedure for raising an aircraft off the ground at multiple points during maintenance, and what considerations should be made when using built-in jack pads?
answer: Normal jacking procedures involve lifting one main wheel at a time.  This procedure is best accomplished using a floor jack in conjunction with the built-in jack pad . CAUTION: Jacking both wheels simultaneously at built-in jack pads is not recommended. When using built-in jack pad, flexibility of the main gear strut will cause the main wheel to slide inboard as the wheel is raised, tilting the jack. If this occurs, the jack must be lowered for a second operation.When the airplane needs to be raised off the ground at all points, the following procedure should be used.
